title: DB transaction only + fire-and-forget side effect (blueprint arm B0; registry baseline db-transaction-fire-and-forget)
venue: CLARA 2027 DSN blueprint (in-project control arm over one ACID transaction)
algorithm_class: Weak control: single ACID transaction commits clinical row + decision receipt, side-effect record sent after commit with no durability coupling
supported_guarantee: Guarantees atomicity and durability of the row+receipt pair inside one database boundary (commit ordering per PostgreSQL WAL discipline); it does NOT guarantee the side-effect record survives a crash between COMMIT and the fire-and-forget send, which is exactly the orphan-clinical-write window RQ1 measures.
limitations_vs_candidate: It is deliberately the weak control, not a competitor: no outbox, no idempotent consumer, no reconciliation - a crash in the post-commit window orphans the side effect and a duplicate replay double-sends it, so it bounds from below what any credible B1 achieves; the parity fixture evaluation/venue2027/dsn/fixtures/fire_and_forget_parity.json is declared but the arm does not exist in this worktree (evaluation/venue2027/dsn is absent), so the honest status is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN.
mechanism_analysis: Strongest competing explanation for the strawman version of RQ1 and mandatory weak control per the blueprint baseline table: its role is to demonstrate that a solved single-boundary primitive (the ACID commit) leaves the joint row+receipt+side-effect outcome underivable, so RQ1's orphan clinical writes are expected to appear here; it must be implemented faithfully (never rebranded as B1) and per the pre-registered falsification rule if B0 alone already shows zero joint-inconsistency events across the 48x4x3x5 design the C1 claim collapses to an application note; the in-project port is absent from this worktree so the ledger records UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN rather than pretending a run.

title: PostgreSQL atomic write + transactional outbox + idempotent consumer (blueprint arm B1; registry baseline postgres-outbox-idempotent-consumer)
venue: CLARA 2027 DSN blueprint (actual PostgreSQL 16.9 REL_16_9 + transactional-outbox pattern)
algorithm_class: Strong practical baseline: atomic multi-table write (row + receipt + outbox insert) in one PostgreSQL transaction, at-least-once relay, consumer dedup keyed by stable operation ID
supported_guarantee: Guarantees crash-atomic persistence of all three records at the database boundary and exactly-once-forwarded application effect via operation-ID dedup (outbox pattern); pinned upstream postgres/postgres tag REL_16_9 commit 6e4ab1b69197e2756192a1019439aebacdea5497 (git ls-remote verified 2026-11-15) with Elle checker jepsen-io/elle v0.2.8 pinned as independent oracle side.
limitations_vs_candidate: This is the pre-registered falsification arm: it enforces joint durability only at commit time and provides no explicit INDETERMINATE terminal state, no consent-epoch binding in the receipt check, and no joint-outcome reconciliation across a crash window that cuts between relay send and consumer dedup ledger persist; if B1 passes the Elle-compatible oracle with zero RQ1/RQ2 violations and equal/better RTO p99 and fsync cost, the new-mechanism-superiority claim is discarded per the novelty contract C2 rule.
mechanism_analysis: Strongest competing explanation for RQ1-RQ3 and the arm the blueprint REQUIRES to be fully implemented under equal budget: PostgreSQL is real runnable upstream pinned at a verified revision and the registry declares it ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM with a parity fixture (evaluation/venue2027/dsn/fixtures/outbox_idempotent_parity.json); available_code=yes records verified upstream availability of the DB engine and pattern source while the in-project harness is still to be built, keeping the ledger honest - the study must run this arm fully or record NOT_RUN_EXTERNAL, and any superiority claim survives only if B1 measurably fails a joint invariant under fault injection.

title: Durable workflow/saga with compensation and stable operation IDs (blueprint arm B2; registry baseline durable-workflow-saga-compensation)
venue: CLARA 2027 DSN blueprint (Temporal Python SDK 1.19.0 durable-execution engine)
algorithm_class: Strong operational baseline: durable workflow execution with event-sourced history, compensation (saga) activities, and stable operation/workflow IDs surviving worker crashes
supported_guarantee: Guarantees durable workflow state via event history persistence and deterministic replay, at-least-once activity dispatch with idempotent apply keyed to stable IDs, and compensation rolls back user-visible effects; upstream temporalio tag 1.19.0 commit 11e8650c7c8b89af45fab328e400d2fd5a9af16c (git ls-remote verified 2026-11-15; engine/version recorded per-run per blueprint requirement).
limitations_vs_candidate: Recoverability is scoped to the workflow engine's own history store: the joint outcome of clinical row + decision receipt + side-effect record is consistent only insofar as all three are funneled through activities, and a crash window between an activity's external side effect and its history-recorded completion still yields an INDETERMINATE that the engine surfaces as retry rather than as an auditable terminal joint outcome; no consent-epoch reconciliation exists, so if B2 attains zero duplicate effects and correct indeterminate handling at equal revocation coverage, C3's necessity claim is discarded per the RQ2 falsification rule.
mechanism_analysis: Strongest competing explanation for RQ2 and RQ3-recovery-cost: Temporal is the canonical published durable-execution system with runnable pinned upstream, so the candidate must beat it on duplicate-side-effect and causal-order invariants under at-least-once replay + concurrent consent revocation or withdraw; available_code=yes records verified upstream availability (parity fixture evaluation/venue2027/dsn/fixtures/saga_compensation_parity.json declared, harness to be built); per registry notes the unit-test harness uses the Temporal test-server only, and any claim beyond engine-scope recoverability is exactly what the study must test, never assume.

title: All File Systems Are Not Created Equal: On the Complexity of Crafting Crash-Consistent Applications
algorithm_class: Empirical study of application-level crash-consistency update protocols over file-system persistence properties (fsync ordering)
supported_guarantee: Documents that widely deployed systems (databases, key-value stores, version control) carry 60 crash vulnerabilities because correctness depends on subtle per-filesystem persistence properties; it defines the fsync/durability discipline any recovery layer silently assumes and the crash-window vocabulary (rename, unlink, truncate orderings) that DSN fault windows generalize to transaction boundaries.
limitations_vs_candidate: It analyzes update protocols over POSIX file systems, not transactional semantics across a row + receipt + side-effect record triad: no isolation oracle, no duplicate-delivery model, no INDETERMINATE terminal state, and no reconciliation of three independent persistence boundaries - it supplies the crash-cut-point methodology (window enumeration over persistence orderings), which the DSN study lifts from file-system operations to commit/relay/revoke orderings, but it proposes no recovery mechanism and therefore cannot itself deliver the joint recoverability outcome.
mechanism_analysis: Strongest competing explanation for the durability-boundary assumption underlying B0/B1: if published evidence already shows the joint triad is recoverable by plain fsync discipline alone the RQ1 crash windows would reduce to known application-level update-protocol bugs; the OSDI 14 paper ships no maintained official reference repository (utsaslab tool repos for chipmunk/CrashMonkey exist but ALICE itself has no pinnable upstream release to cite as code), so the honest ledger status is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN - it is cited for its crash-window method and its 60-vulnerability evidence that persistence discipline alone does not deliver recoverability.

title: ARIES: A Transaction Recovery Method Supporting Fine-Granularity Locking and Partial Rollbacks Using Write-Ahead Logging
algorithm_class: Write-ahead logging with steal/no-force buffer management, fuzzy checkpoints, and repeating-history redo followed by undo of loser transactions
supported_guarantee: Guarantees transactional durability and atomicity after any crash: WAL records are flushed before the corresponding data pages, and restart replays (redo) all committed work and rolls back (undo) in-flight work, giving the canonical commit/abort determinism that underpins every B0/B1 durability claim in this study.
limitations_vs_candidate: It recovers a SINGLE database to a consistent prefix of its own log; it has no concept of a joint outcome spanning three persistence boundaries (row, receipt, side-effect record), no user-visible INDETERMINATE terminal state exposed to an application or auditor, and no duplicate-delivery or consent-revocation reconciliation - ARIES determinism is precisely what makes the residual disagreement in RQ1 an application/journal-layer problem rather than a storage-engine one, which is the gap the candidate journal occupies.
mechanism_analysis: Boundary comparator for the RQ3 fsync/WAL cost model and the strongest competing explanation that WAL recovery already solves C1: the ARIES paper is the canonical reference (verified via Crossref DOI resolution, ACM TODS 17(1) pp. 94-162, 1992) that single-store crash recovery yields a deterministic committed-or-aborted prefix, so any joint-inconsistency the study observes on real PostgreSQL (itself ARIES-lineage) cannot be blamed on the storage engine; the 1992 paper has no executable reference implementation to pin, so the honest status is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN and its role is to fix the recovery-semantics boundary the journal must out-perform.

title: Reconciliation safety journal (candidate arm: versioned receipt vs committed row + outbox receipt + consent epoch)
venue: CLARA 2027 DSN blueprint (candidate B4: recoverable-outcome function over synthetic-dsn-2027 fault-injection histories)
algorithm_class: Candidate mechanism: append-only reconciliation journal checked by a recoverable-outcome function that returns COMMITTED, REJECTED, or INDETERMINATE until reconcilable ground truth exists across the three persistence boundaries
supported_guarantee: Claimed (not yet demonstrated): fewer joint-inconsistency outcomes than engineered baselines with bounded ambiguity - every crash window resolves to an explicit auditable terminal state; invalid or ambiguous evidence is never promoted to a positive outcome and retries are keyed to immutable operation IDs; all thresholds and observed values enter only via artifacts/venue2027/dsn/<run_id>/manifest.json after protocol freeze.
limitations_vs_candidate: It is the candidate itself, not a comparator: no run exists, no crash window has been injected, and the pre-registered falsification rule applies at full strength - if B1 (outbox) or B2 (saga) achieves identical invariants with equal or better RTO p99 and fsync cost, the superiority claim is discarded and negative equivalence reported instead (novelty contract C2/RQ3).
mechanism_analysis: Candidate anchor recorded for falsification transparency: this is the arm RQ1-RQ3 exist to test against B0/B1/B2/B3-fsync and B5-mono-journal, so its guarantee is deliberately phrased as a hypothesis with the 48x4x3x5 crash-window design as the designated adversarial experiment; until DSN-X06 (reconcile journal) and the fault-injection runner execute on real PostgreSQL, the honest status is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN, and per the cross-study firewall this arm consumes no frozen E15-E22 archive, no COMPSAC contention results and no IFIP replay evidence - the study must never present this row as a comparator that has been beaten or has run.

title: Single monotonic journal (weak control arm: one undifferentiated log for row + receipt + side-effect claims; control for B4)
venue: CLARA 2027 DSN blueprint (in-project control arm B5: single-stream journal without tri-state reconciliation)
algorithm_class: Weak control: a single append-only journal records all persistence events in one stream; recovery replays it without cross-checking receipt-vs-row-vs-consent-epoch consistency
supported_guarantee: Guarantees an auditable ordered record of persistence events (Certificate-Transparency-style append-only integrity of the journal itself) and deterministic replay; it does NOT detect a receipt whose row never committed, a side effect sent without a receipt, or a consent epoch revoked mid-window - the replay is faithful to the log, not to the joint outcome.
limitations_vs_candidate: It is the internal control separating structure from semantics in the candidate: single-log integrity (per ct9162) is not reconciliation, so B5 isolates exactly the delta the recoverable-outcome function adds over mere journaling; its falsification role is symmetric to B0 - if B5 matches B4's joint-inconsistency rate the tri-state reconciliation contributes nothing and C1/C2 collapse; the arm does not exist in this worktree so the honest status is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN.
mechanism_analysis: Mandatory internal control and the strongest competing explanation for the journal component alone: it tests whether an append-only log without the recoverable-outcome function already achieves the safety numbers, i.e. whether the mechanism reduces to ct9162-style log integrity plus replay; it must be implemented with equal budget like every blueprint arm and reported NOT_RUN_EXTERNAL if it cannot run - never silently dropped, since a missing weak control would make the B4 comparison unfalsifiable; per the firewall it reuses no sibling-venue evidence.

title: Certificate Transparency Version 2.0
algorithm_class: Certificate Transparency v2.0: append-only Merkle Tree Hash log with signed tree heads, inclusion proofs and monotonic log growth
supported_guarantee: Verifiable append-only logging (RFC 9162 Sec. 2): any auditor can verify entry inclusion against a signed tree head and silent truncation or rewriting is detectable; the log is a gossip-verified integrity substrate, not a transactional store.
limitations_vs_candidate: Provides integrity and public auditability of log contents and nothing about joint-outcome semantics: an append-only log does not reconcile the entries it holds, does not define COMMITTED/REJECTED/INDETERMINATE outcomes for a crashed writer, does not bind a consent epoch, and supports no idempotent replay of external side effects - exactly the boundary between transparency logging (this row) and the reconciliation journal (candidate B4) that the study must demonstrate rather than assert.
mechanism_analysis: Strongest competing explanation for the journal-integrity component of the candidate and required registry comparator: RFC 9162 is the canonical proof that verifiable append-only logs give integrity without reconciliation semantics, so a reviewer can demand the study show the INDETERMINATE discipline adds value beyond a CT-style log; an IETF standard has no runnable implementation to cite as an arm (CT log implementations exist but none is the standard), so the honest status is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN - its guarantee bounds what log integrity alone supports and anchors the B5 control's design.

title: Elle: Inferring Isolation Anomalies from Experimental Observations
algorithm_class: Black-box transaction-history anomaly checker: infers isolation anomalies (G0/G1/G1c, lost writes, duplicate effects) from observed histories via ellement/list-append consistency checks
supported_guarantee: Infers real anomalies purely from exported execution histories without instrumenting the SUT internals (Elle list-append/txn descriptions); pinned upstream jepsen-io/elle (repo live, HEAD 4e359e597c52938b0afebb8bc42273914d68a424 at check 2026-11-15; registry pins v0.2.8 commit 2843344620c7d0653eef1c20728aa8580a05f505) as the study's independent oracle side.
limitations_vs_candidate: Elle checks isolation and outcome anomalies WITHIN one exported history but defines no joint COMMITTED/REJECTED/INDETERMINATE recoverable-outcome function across three persistence boundaries, no consent-revocation semantics, and no recovery-time metric - it is the oracle instrument, not a recovery mechanism, so it validates RQ1/RQ2 histories yet cannot itself make the joint outcome recoverable; the oracle reviewer must not reuse candidate code per the blueprint independence rule.
mechanism_analysis: Independent-oracle anchor for RQ1 and RQ2: the blueprint mandates a Jepsen/Elle-compatible history export and this row records the pinned runnable upstream (git ls-remote verified 2026-11-15) whose anomaly inference defines what a disagreement IS before any candidate is compared; available_code=yes with ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM records verified upstream availability for oracle fidelity, while the in-project export harness (DSN-X08 elle_export) is still to be built - the ledger keeps the oracle-side availability separate from arm execution status so the oracle can never be presented as a beaten comparator.

title: Speedy Transactions in Multicore In-Memory Databases
algorithm_class: Silo: epoch-based optimistic concurrency control with per-tuple versioned reads and commit-time-batched validation (no centralized lock table or timestamp allocation on the commit path)
supported_guarantee: Guarantees serializable multi-core OLTP transactions inside ONE store via optimistic validation and commit-time batching; registry relation: serializable optimistic concurrency, scalable in-memory baseline, not a health-specific disclosure mechanism.
limitations_vs_candidate: Silo's serializability is single-store concurrency control: it says nothing about crash recovery of a joint outcome across independent persistence boundaries, provides no duplicate-delivery or consent-revocation semantics, and its in-memory design is orthogonal to the durability windows RQ1 enumerates - a serializable execution is exactly the precondition under which any residual disagreement must come from the crash/reconciliation layer, not from CC, which is why it is the study's CC-boundary reference and not a competitor to the journal.
mechanism_analysis: Strongest competing explanation that database-side CC alone already prevents the anomalies RQ1 observes: citing Silo (SOSP 2013, DOI verified via Crossref; no official code release exists to pin, per the shared baseline registry's silo-style entry which declares UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN) lets the study show serializable CC inside one store is orthogonal to post-crash joint recoverability - the falsified alternative would be that RQ1 events are actually CC anomalies; the honest ledger status is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN since only a paper-described re-implementation exists in the sibling COMPSAC registry, never Silo upstream code.
